scope: Advisory semantic judging of Jev decision-layer outputs on the synthetic corpus in this directory. The rubric governs how a judge may score model behavior; it never rewrites outcomes, labels, or deterministic test results.

binding.advisoryOnly: Judge scores are advisory observability signals and NEVER replace reference labels (AC-16). The corpus labels (acceptable/unacceptable with labelProvenance) remain the only release-gating ground truth. A judge score must never be written into a reference label field, and a judge/reference disagreement must never silently override the reference.
binding.agreementIsNotAccuracy: Agreement with the incumbent baseline is NOT accuracy (AC-15). Counting identical selections between two systems says nothing about correctness against the corpus labels. Any judge report must keep agreement counts structurally separate from correctness metrics.
binding.securityTestsAreDeterministic: Deterministic security and validation checks (label-vocabulary rejection, provenance gating, dataset digest, transport refusal rules) are pass/fail and are never judged. A judge may never soften, reinterpret, or waive a failed deterministic check.
binding.noRawPayloads: Judge inputs are bounded machine tokens and numbers from adapter-validated evidence. Raw provider payloads, prompts, and credential material are never judge inputs and are never retained in reports.

criteria: Each permitted domain carries an independent yesProbability in [0,1]; the values are never normalized into a distribution.
A high probability on a domain the corpus labels unacceptable is a judge finding to report, never a relabeling of the case.
Evidence with status unavailable and a failure reason is scored as non-answered, never guessed or interpolated.
route-domains.notes: Reference labels are corpus domain names. The evaluation CLI derives a selection deterministically (argmax yesProbability, ties keep corpus declaration order); a judge scores the full score vector, not only the argmax.

criteria: Exactly one intent label from the fixed five-label vocabulary is chosen.
Per-label probabilities are complete over the criteria and each lies in [0,1].
The chosen label is the argmax of the returned probabilities.
An off-vocabulary choice or probability is a validation failure, not a judge reclassification opportunity.
classify-client-intent.notes: Reference labels come from the corpus acceptable/unacceptable lists. Judges may flag near-miss distributions (for example a narrow margin between the chosen and an unacceptable label) as advisory findings only.

criteria: Each of the five judgment aspects (mutationRequested, targetUnambiguous, valueUnambiguous, sufficientEvidence, clarificationRequired) is answered independently in [0,1].
The judgments are never normalized into a distribution.
The corpus evaluates the resulting binary outcome; judges may score the full judgment vector but must not collapse it into the outcome label.
evaluate-clarification.notes: The evaluation CLI binarizes with the deterministic convention clarificationRequired >= 0.5 maps to clarification-required; this threshold is an evaluation-harness convention, not a production policy, and judges must report raw judgments alongside any outcome opinion.

criteria: The answer is one of the supplied candidate labels or the fixed alternatives none / insufficient_evidence.
Per-label probabilities are complete over the criteria and each lies in [0,1].
The chosen label is the argmax of the returned probabilities.
A match outcome must name a candidate from the supplied choice set; no candidate may be invented.
rank-candidates.notes: The corpus evaluates the outcome token, not a specific production choice set. The live runner executes these cases with a single deterministic placeholder candidate (label candidate-1, no facts); scores under this convention measure the pinned model on the synthetic scenario only and must never be presented as production candidate-ranking accuracy.
